transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2028-04-11 15:00 PDT
- Duration: ~62 minutes
- Attendees: Jared (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Liam, Sara, Omar, Hannah (ZephyrSearch)

Auto-summary (auto gen, may be imperfect):
Jared gave quick intro, Priya demoed hosted embeddings + rerank flow end-to-end; customer asked about latency SLOs, token cost, and data residency. Talked about using prefix caching and batching to reduce cost. Customer asked about SOC 2 and VPC options; we clarified hosted API with audit logs vs Dedicated/Private.

00:00 Jared: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick intros - I'm Jared with Redwood, lead AE for search.
00:07 Liam: Hi, Liam here, head of search at ZephyrSearch. We run a hosted search infra and looking to add semantic reranking to our results.
00:12 Sara: Sara, eng manager, will own integration.
00:18 Priya: Hi, I'm Priya, will run the demo - I'll show embeddings pipeline, vector store pattern, candidate gen, then the reranker endpoint.
01:02 Priya: Ok starting the demo — first, embeddings. We'll call /v1/embeddings with a short snippet to get vector for query. Example: "best noise-cancelling headphones under $200". Returned 768-d vector; note we support multiple dims depending on model.
01:25 Omar: quick Q — what model do you use by default, and can we pin to an open model?
01:30 Priya: Default is a Redwood-curated embed model (redwood-embed-v2), you can pin to a specific model version or swap to open models we host. For production we recommend verifying performance on your set; we can do that in the pilot.
02:05 Priya: Candidate generation patterns — we demo nearest neighbor on a vector store (we used a simple FAISS-backed example for demo) to pull top 100 then rerank.
02:35 Sara: Do you recommend 100? our current infra tops at 50 for latency concerns.
02:40 Priya: 50 is common too. The tradeoff is recall vs reranker compute. We showed 100 to demonstrate improved recall; with our batching and prefix cache you can keep latency within SLOs even with larger candidate sets.
03:10 Priya: Next, the reranker endpoint — we send the query+candidate doc pairs to /v1/rerank, model returns a score and explanation token highlights. Response includes a score float and optional token-level attribution.
03:34 Liam: Attribution would be very helpful for search relevance tuning — is that part of hosted offering?
03:40 Priya: Yes it's part of the response on certain models; we flagged that in Console too under per-request traces. It's best-effort and the token highlights sometimes get noisy depending on the model.
04:15 Priya: Demo: I paste an example query and top 5 candidates. You can see the reranker reorders results and we show delta in nDCG.
04:50 Hannah: small nit — are embeddings stored on our side or yours?
04:55 Priya: For hosted API embeddings are stored in Redwood's managed store unless you opt for us to ship vectors to your S3/managed vector store. We also support not persisting embeddings (ephemeral) for PII-sensitive flows.
05:20 Omar: security Q — SOC2, keys, encryption at rest?
05:25 Jared: We are SOC2 Type II; keys are managed via KMS with customer-managed key options for Dedicated/Private, plus TLS in transit and at-rest encryption. Audit logs available in Console.
06:02 Sara: Does hosted API support SSO / SCIM for team management?
06:07 Jared: Yes, SSO/SAML and SCIM provisioning for enterprise accounts; RBAC in Console. For VPC/private deployments we can also integrate with customer IdP.
06:45 Priya: Back to performance — we talked about batching: you can batch multiple rerank pairs into one request for throughput efficiency. Also prefix/KV cache reduces cost for repeated contexts e.g., user profile.
07:20 Omar: how do you handle long documents? Our docs are multi-section and often 3k tokens.
07:26 Priya: We recommend chunking with semantic chunk size ~500-700 tokens and storing chunks with metadata. For rerank, we prefer candidate passages sized to fit into model context; longer passages are truncated or summarized.
08:00 Priya: Console demo now — show request traces, token-level cost breakdown, per-route lat/throughput, and Optimize suggestions that recommend batching size and quantized model variants.
08:38 Priya: The Optimize tab flagged a suggestion: switch reranker model to quantized variant for 2x cost reduction with ~2% quality delta in our internal benchmarks.
09:10 Liam: If we wanted dedicated GPUs for predictable latency, what's the path?
09:15 Jared: Dedicated is a reserved capacity offering — predictable throughput, SLA-backed latency. We can size a pool based on your qps and tail latency targets. Private (VPC/on-prem) available for data residency needs.
10:00 Sara: For an initial pilot we'd like to test on dev dataset (2k docs) and run 1k queries to measure nDCG and P95 latency.
10:08 Priya: Great, we can run that — I'll run the benchmark with your sample set once you share it. We'll provide a spreadsheet with latency, cost, and quality metrics.
10:45 Omar: cost question — how are you charging for rerank? per-token or per-request?
10:50 Jared: Hosted API pricing is per-token for generation/rerank and per-embedding unit for embed calls. For rerank we show token breakdown in Console for each request and Optimize helps estimate unit costs. For Dedicated we provide reserved compute pricing.
11:25 Liam: Any limits on concurrency for hosted?
11:29 Jared: There are soft rate limits by default; we can increase for pilots. For very high concurrency we recommend Dedicated.
11:52 Priya: Demo note: sometimes transcripts mislabel product names — e.g., KV cache gets transcribed weirdly; ignore minor typos.
12:18 Priya: Quick deep-dive on rerank scoring: we return normalized scores; you can combine them with your base BM25 score using linear combination in ranking pipeline. Many customers do a weighted blend (0.7 BM25 + 0.3 rerank) to keep recall.
13:05 Sara: Do you support online learning or feedback loops?
13:10 Priya: We don't host model retraining in hosted API; you can ship signals (clicks) to our Optimize ingestion or use your pipeline to fine-tune models. For online personalization we support storing user vectors and performing personalization at query time.
13:48 Omar: latency numbers — what P95 can we expect for rerank on hosted?
13:52 Priya: For small candidate sets (<=50) and a mid-size rerank model, P95 is typically 120-230ms depending on region and model. We showed a demo trace at ~150ms P95.
14:22 Liam: that's acceptable for our web latency budgets. Do you have examples of customers in ads/search space?
14:28 Jared: Yes, a couple of search-first customers — we can share redacted case studies.
15:05 Hannah: Data residency — we need logs not leave EU region. Is that possible?
15:10 Jared: We have regional hosting options and Private deployment for strict residency. For hosted we can configure regionally where data is stored, but complete EU-only controls are better served by Private.
16:00 Priya: Demo wrap-up — I'll drop a link to the benchmark template and a short runbook for integration.
16:20 Liam: sounds good — timeline wise we'd like pilot next week if possible.
16:25 Jared: We'll target a pilot kickoff the week of 2028-04-17 pending data.
16:33 Priya: Recap of action items in Console we'll put in CRM too.
16:50 Jared: Any final Qs?
16:58 Sara: Not from me, thanks for the clear walk-through.
17:05 Liam: thanks everyone.

Closing (end of recording): 16:58 - roughly 62 minutes recorded.
